text:
marie: quick heads-up — I ran a microprofile on the ingress framer for streaming HTTP/2 traffic and we're seeing ~2.4ms extra per-512B chunk on hosted us-west (model=gpt-small-8k, kernel=v2).

raj: hosted only or also dedicated?

marie: hosted. replica pool A. observed across ~1200 streams over 10m.

taylor: do you have the flame/sample hotspots?

marie: pasted the hot functions from pprof: 
```
ingress_framer_handle_chunk        2.4ms
parse_http2_frame                 1.7ms
decode_headers                    0.9ms
kv_cache_lookup                   0.05ms
```

olivia: parse_http2_frame at 1.7ms per chunk is surprising — are we allocating per-chunk?

raj: good question. I skimmed framer.go — looks like we do: `for _, c := range chunks { r := bytes.NewReader(c); parse(r) }` which allocs a new reader and triggers tiny GC pressure per iteration.

marie: yep, exact snippet: `for _, c := range chunks { r := bytes.NewReader(c); headers := parseHTTP2Headers(r); processChunk(headers, c.payload) }` — that'll reparse headers and re-create backing objects for every chunk even when headers are unchanged.

taylor: we also do `json.Unmarshal` for request metadata on every chunk in some codepaths (legacy wire format). That explains attritional CPU.

olivia: proposed fixes: 1) only parse headers on START_FRAME or when header-flag present, 2) reuse a single bytes.Reader (or zero-copy slice view) across chunks, 3) move json.Unmarshal to initial frame and cache struct in stream context.

raj: implementing a micro-PR: reuse reader + add header-parsed boolean on stream state. rough diff: 
```
// before
for _, c := range chunks {
  r := bytes.NewReader(c)
  h := parseHTTP2Headers(r)
  handle(h, c)
}
// after
r := bytes.NewReader(nil)
for _, c := range chunks {
  r.Reset(c)
  if !stream.headersParsed && hasHeaderFlag(c) {
    stream.headers = parseHTTP2Headers(r)
    stream.headersParsed = true
  }
  handle(stream.headers, c)
}
```

marie: also added a KV cache hit check — if kv_cache_lookup is inlined we can avoid a tiny syscall for misses by using a fast-path map read.

taylor: nice. Can you also add a bench for chunk sizes (128B/512B/2KB) and both http1 and http2 framing? We saw the delta amplify at small chunks.

raj: will do. I'll push the bench and a small patch today.

olivia: watch out for gRPC: grpc with http2 windowing merges frames; ensure we don't break streaming unit tests.

raj: good call — I'll run the integration tests.

(2h later)

deploy-bot: canary deploy completed for branch `framer-opt` on pool A — latency median for streaming calls decreased by ~1.9ms at 512B chunk size :tada:

marie: amazing — thanks everyone. I'll follow up with a perf writeup and a few charts for the console.

taylor: add a note to ops runbook about the header-cache bit, so on rollback we don't forget the guard.

olivia: filed a small regression test to assert headersParsed state across reconnections.

raj: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/421 — includes bench results and small refactor.

marie: closing the thread here, will pin the results in #eng-runtime-perf for reference. :white_check_mark:
